data.narrative:
Neuralink, a private-stage AI & Software company founded by Elon Musk and colleagues, has raised $1.3B+ to date. The AI & Software sector contains 16 identifiable peers; however, the company's unique technology focus and capital intensity limit strict comparable peer availability. The narrow peer set comprises 1 public comparable (Palantir Technologies, ticker PLTR) and 8 private peers including Waymo, Scale AI, Figure AI, and Reflection AI.

Standard peer-median valuation was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow peer set. Only 2 same-stage AI & Software companies met initial filters, falling short of the minimum 3 datapoints required for robust triangulation. Expanding to all-sector medians would introduce substantial sector heterogeneity and misrepresent risk and growth profiles specific to frontier AI infrastructure.

The analysis cannot reliably support a point estimate given data constraints. Key uncertainties include: (1) the degree to which Palantir's public valuation multiples transfer to earlier-stage, hardware-centric AI infrastructure; (2) commercial timelines and clinical validation risk for Neuralink's core neurotechnology platform; and (3) divergent revenue models and scale trajectories among the private peer set. Any valuation estimate at this stage would require subjective assumptions regarding technology risk premiums and comparability adjustments not supported by the available dataset. Additional comparable transaction data or company guidance on path-to-revenue would strengthen analytical rigor.
